Maintenance Report — MNT-0161-001

Asset: WELL-0161 (NE-08 Well 161, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: rod string Work started: 15 Sep 2023 08:00 · Finished: 27 Sep 2023 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 284 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0161-0001 on 2023-09-14 Report written: 29 Sep 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0161-0001 showed the wellhead at 40.9 °C with the air at 31.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 10 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started, but it was not written down (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Sucker rods7,458
Rod couplings1,864
Fishing tool rental3,108
Labour (company crew)5,492
Total17,922

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 3 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.
  • HSE to follow up on the WS-01 item above with the crew.

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0161-007

Asset: WELL-0161 (NE-08 Well 161, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 Jul 2024 08:00 · Finished: 07 Aug 2024 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 300 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0161-0045 on 2024-07-25 Report written: 07 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0161-0045 showed the wellhead at 49.3 °C with the air at 38.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0161-007 (WS-06).

Notes and recommendations

  • Check the gearbox oil level monthly on this unit.
  • Used oil and pads shipped as oily waste.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0161-014

Asset: WELL-0161 (NE-08 Well 161, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 05 Sep 2025 08:00 · Finished: 05 Sep 2025 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0161-0100 on 2025-09-04 Report written: 06 Sep 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0161-0100 at 10:15 on 2025-09-04 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.3% of the pad area, estimated 1.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 395 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 316 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.2 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0161-014 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.65% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Line pipe and fittings1,758
Absorbents and berms781
Soil hauling and disposal1,367
Labour (company crew and contractor)4,190
Total8,096

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 1 ppm
WS-04MetPermit issued; gas test 0% LEL
WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours
WS-06MetOily waste manifested to an approved site
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)
SR-02MetContained about 1.4 hours after discovery (limit 4 hours)
SR-04MetSpill recorded with volume and area (moderate class)
HSE noticeMetHSE notified 23 hours after discovery (company limit 72 hours for moderate spills)
SR-03MetCleaned to below 1.0% TPH; agency verification applies only to reportable spills

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
